title: Micro-ops huddle: routing + auth checklist and notes (Apr 21 2026)
content:
Purpose
- Short micro-huddle notes capturing blocking items and immediate checklist for routing/auth/quotas ahead of tomorrow's handoff to on-call. Keep actionable, mention owners and clear next steps.

Attendees
- Aisha (owner)
- Marco
- Sofia
- Diego
- Note: Erin from SRE was invited but could not join; added follow-ups.

Top-level summary (2 lines)
- No customer-facing outage. Small regression in route selection causing 95th p95 latency increase from 220ms -> 360ms for model shard groups A1 between 09:30–10:15 PDT 2026-04-20. Root cause: allocator did uneven shard placement under sticky routing experiment.
- Mitigation: rolled back routing experiment at 10:22, autoscale policy tightened. Action items below.

Observed signals and quick metrics
- Latency signal: p50 steady, p95 spike for shards serving seq_len>1024.
- Error rates: 5xx remained at baseline (~0.03%). No spike in client errors.
- Quota burn: Dedicated tier saw short burst of quota usage due to replays; resolved after rollback.
- Telemetry pages: Dashboard "routing-p95-by-shard" shows spike window annotated.

Incident timeline (short)
- 09:26 PDT: First p95 alerts on dashboard (automated tag).
- 09:30–09:50: Engineers investigate; hypothesis: sticky routing variant 3 introduced uneven placement for A1 causing tokenization-related amplification.
- 09:52: Confirmed correlation with experiment rollout logs (controlplane-experiments).
- 10:22: Experiment rolled back to sticky-v2. Immediate p95 reduction by 40% over next 6 minutes.
- 10:35: Autoscale policy tightened (min-instances +1) for A1 group to absorb burst.
- 11:00: Monitoring stabilized; no customer complaints.

Root cause hypothesis
- Sticky routing v3 had a placement heuristic change (favored node affinity over available kv-cache size) which concentrated large-seq requests onto a subset of nodes with smaller KV cache allocations. Result: more frequent rematerialization and higher latencies.
- Secondary factor: a recently merged scheduler optimization (PR #7842) changed a fallback window; combined with the above produced the spike.

Decisions made during huddle
- Immediate rollback of sticky routing v3 -> sticky-v2 (done). Owner: Marco.
- Add an invariant check in experiments controller: if net-kv-cache-available < threshold for a shard, do not prefer affinity. Owner: Sofia. Jira: PLT-1329.
- Short-term autoscale policy change for A1 group (+1 min instance) to be kept for 48 hours. Owner: Diego.
- Add p95-by-seq-len alert to catch future unevenness earlier. Owner: Aisha.

Action items (concrete)
- Aisha: Draft a short postmortem stub and link to this doc. Due: 2026-04-23. Tag: internal mailing list.
- Marco: Revert rolled-back experiment in controlplane-experiments and add a gated canary for node-affinity changes. PR reference: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7842. Due: 2026-04-24.
- Sofia: Implement invariant in experiments controller to check kv-cache headroom. Add unit tests + integration test. Jira: PLT-1329. Due: 2026-04-28.
- Diego: Adjust autoscale policy for A1 and monitor for 48h, report on utilization in next standup. Due: 2026-04-23.
- Erin (SRE): Add a runbook snippet for sticky-routing fallbacks (how to rollback, telemetry to annotate), coordinate with on-call docs. Due: 2026-04-25.

Open questions and discussion points
- How aggressive should canary throttling be for routing-affinity changes that affect KV cache fragmentation? (Marco/Sofia to propose a default throttling profile.)
- Should we introduce a synthetic load test for seq_len distribution extremes? Quick suggestion: nightly job that replays 2% of production requests with seq_len>2048 into a staging pool. Action: Aisha + Diego to prototype.
- Impact surface: Are private deployments (VPC) also subject to the same placement heuristic? Need to check controlplane config syncs for private. Action: Sofia to audit config template replication.

Quick checklist for on-call handoff (what to say in Slack + bridge)
- TL;DR: p95 spike on A1 due to sticky routing v3 -> rolled back to v2; autoscale increased. No customer impact. Keep eyes on p95-by-seq-len and quota burn for dedicated tier.
- Commands to run: 
  - Check experiment state: kubectl -n controlplane get experiments controlplane-experiments -o yaml | grep sticky
  - Force rollback (if needed): ./scripts/experiments/rollback.sh sticky-routing-v3
  - View p95 by shard: dashboards/routing-p95-by-shard (Grafana link in linked_artifacts)
- Quick guide: if p95 resurges for same shard group, escalate to platform-ops on-call and tag "routing-regression".

Notes from engineering deep-dive (tech details)
- Experiment controller code path: selection->affinity_score->kv_headroom_calc. Current kv_headroom_calc uses static threshold per model-family; need dynamic value based on shard's current cache budget.
- PR #7842 changed fallback-window from 2s -> 6s to permit transient backpressure smoothing; this interacts poorly with affinity because it increased time-on-node for rematerialization windows.
- Suggest adding metrics: kv_headroom_bytes_gauge, node-affinity-moves_count. Add these to controlplane telemetry for better correlation.

Follow-up meeting proposals
- Deep-dive session next Wed (2026-04-28) to review fixes and test results (Marco + Sofia + Diego + SRE).
- Postmortem draft review on Thu (2026-04-23) 10:00 PDT.

Miscellaneous notes (scratchpad)
- Idea: when promoting a routing variant, check a preflight job that validates per-node cache headroom across active nodes. Could be done by reusing the allocator's probe API.
- Slack snippets to copy into incident channel: "Routing p95 spike; rolled back sticky-v3; monitoring; no customer impact. See doc: <link>"
- Related tickets: PLT-1298 (allocator fragmentation investigation), PLT-1307 (autoscale policy tuning for ded tier), PLT-1329 (experiments invariant).

Closing
- This doc is the canonical micro-handoff record for the Apr 21 checks. If you modify any of the action items, update the due date and owner here. Keep short notes inline rather than creating scattered follow-ups.

- End of notes.
